nodes.name: NiS Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.2448 g nickel acetate (99 wt%, Alfa Aesar) and 0.2300 g thioacetamide (99 wt%, Alfa Aesar) were dissolved in 35 mL deionized water. After stirring, the mixture was poured into a 50 ml autoclave with a piece of pretreated carbon paper (0.5 × 1.5 cm²). The growth was carried out at 120 °C in an electric oven for 12 h. After the autoclave cooled down naturally to room temperature, the samples were removed, washed with deionized water, and then dried in a vacuum oven at room temperature.

nodes.name: Ni3S2/NiO
aliases: mixed phase of Ni3S2 and NiO

nodes.characterization_summary: As-synthesized NiS shows characteristic reflections of hexagonal α-phase NiS. After HER (NiS-40), XRD shows pattern characteristic of Ni3S2 indicating full phase conversion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern shown in Fig. 1a ... characteristic of the hexagonal α-phase of NiS. Figure 1a shows an XRD pattern of the NiS-40 sample, from which a pattern characteristic of Ni3S2 can be identified.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p XPS of as-synthesized NiS characteristic of NiS phase. NiS-40 shows pronounced spectral feature in Ni 2p3/2 region arising from NiO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) of Ni 2p core level in Fig. 1b suggests that the as-synthesized samples are characteristic of the hexagonal α-phase of NiS. The XPS in the Ni 2p3/2 region for the NiS-40 sample exhibits a pronounced spectral feature possibly arising from NiO.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiS particles ~200 nm uniformly coating carbon paper. NiS-40 after 25h shows small NiO clusters anchored on large Ni3S2 particles with lattice spacings 0.21 nm (NiO (200)) and 0.30 nm (Ni3S2 (-110)).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images ... NiS particles with a size of ~200 nm uniformly coating on the carbon paper substrate. The large-area TEM image reveals numerous small NiO clusters anchored onto the large Ni3S2. The HR-TEM image exhibits ... interplanar spacing of 0.21 nm corresponding well to the (200) lattice plane of NiO ... 0.30 nm which matches well with (-110) lattice plane of Ni3S2.

properties.visual_features: dark nanoparticles on light background with blue overlay

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Ni K-edge XAS reveals NiS→Ni3S2 phase transition at -0.27 V vs RHE, S vacancy formation (decreased Ni-S coordination) at more negative potentials in region II, and gradual NiO formation in region III with 13% NiO at +0.50 V and 22% at +1.00 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transition from region I to region II at −0.27 V can be identified as the phase transition NiS→Ni3S2 ... a continuous decrease of the spectral intensity of the white line ... suggests a further reduction ... decrease of the average coordination number of Ni coordinated by S, suggesting the formation of S vacancies ... The spectrum can be fitted with a linear combination of Ni3S2 and an increasing contribution of NiO ... NiO contribution at +0.50 V is about 13%, which further increases to 22% when the sample potential reaches +1.00 V.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Raman confirms NiS→Ni3S2 transition (peaks at 221, 303, 322, 349 cm⁻¹) and NiO formation (peaks at 453, 493, 600, 800, 1060 cm⁻¹) under HER conditions; stable over 25 h at -0.30 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Operando Raman spectroscopy of NiS at different applied voltages ... characteristic peaks assigned to NiS disappear, while the characteristic peaks assigned to Ni3S2 appear at 221, 303, 322, and 349 cm⁻¹ ... newly emerged peaks ... at 453, 493, 600, 800, and 1060 cm⁻¹ can be assigned to NiO ... extended the operando Raman experiment at an applied potential of −0.30 V vs. RHE to 25 h. The results demonstrate Ni3S2 and NiO remain stable.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiS-40 shows higher OH*/(H2O*+OH*) ratio than NiS at 0.5 mbar water vapor indicating stronger water dissociation ability. Water exposure increases Ni-O intensity in Ni 2p3/2 and shows S 2p shoulder from H* adsorption at S sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4b shows the XPS spectra of NiS and NiS-40 ... in the O 1s region ... the ratio (Rdis) of OH* to (H2O* + OH*) in NiS-40 is much higher than that in NiS ... For the NiS-40 sample, water exposure induces a pronounced change in the Ni 2p3/2 ... spectral intensity associated with Ni-O increases significantly ... for S 2p shown in Fig. 4e, after water exposure, a shoulder feature appears at the lower binding energy side.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiS-40 after 25-h chronopotentiometry shows NiO (200) lattice spacing of 0.21 nm and Ni3S2 (-110) lattice spacing of 0.30 nm at interface; elemental mapping confirms O enrichment on NiO clusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Spherical Aberration Corrected Transmission Electron Microscope (SAC-TEM) ... the cluster region has an interplanar spacing of 0.21 nm corresponding well to the (200) lattice plane of NiO, while the other region has an interplanar spacing of 0.30 nm which matches well with (-110) lattice plane of Ni3S2. More importantly, the elemental mapping shows the preferential enrichment of oxygen elements on the small cluster.
